newsitem.title: TAIWAN: U.S. House speaker Gingrich meets Taiwan president.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House speaker Gingrich meets Taiwan president.

text.p: U.S. congressional chief Newt Gingrich met on Wednesday with Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui, a symbolic show of support following his controversial vow that U.S. forces would defend the island from Chinese attack.
"I'm glad to be here," Gingrich told Lee at the start of a meeting in Lee's office broadcast live on Taiwan television.

The visit by Gingrich, the first House of Representatives speaker to visit since Washington switched diplomatic ties to Beijing in 1979, put an intense spotlight on Taiwan-China frictions, seen by Beijing as a key irritant in Sino-U.S. ties.

Gingrich's weekend assertion that U.S. forces would defend the Nationalist-ruled island from attack by the communist mainland sent U.S. officials scurrying to clarify Washington's position and triggered an angry rebuke by Beijing.
Beijing, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949, opposes U.S. arms sales to the island as interference in China's internal affairs.

Beijing, which adamantly opposes contacts between Taiwan's leaders and U.S. officials, briefly downgraded ties with Washington after President Lee was allowed to make a private visit to New York in mid-1995.
U.S. law authorises Washington to offer defensive arms to Taiwan but is ambiguous on whether the United States would come to the Nationalist-ruled island's defence.
